summary.headline: CCL Products Q2 FY27 revenue rose 7.8% to INR1,215.99 crore on 10-15% volume growth, with EBITDA up 9.5% to INR217.3 crore.
summary.overview: Group turnover grew 7.8% YoY to INR1,215.99 crore, with value growth trailing double-digit volume growth because green coffee prices fell. EBITDA rose 9.5% to INR217.3 crore, PBT rose 18.7% to INR150.86 crore and net profit rose about 29% to INR130 crore. H1 turnover was INR2,419.58 crore (+11.6%), H1 EBITDA INR414 crore (+15%) and H1 PAT INR246.96 crore (+42%). Management reiterated full-year guidance of about 15% volume and similar EBITDA growth, with EBITDA per kg held at INR135-140.

segments.name: Domestic branded (Continental)
segments.commentary: Gross domestic turnover of about INR210 crore in Q2, of which brand sales about INR140 crore; branded business growing 25%, driven by volume across GT, MT and e-commerce. FY27 branded guidance of about INR550 crore maintained, with H1 at INR250-260 crore.

segments.name: International branded (Percol and others)
segments.commentary: Percol revenue expected at about INR25-30 crore for FY27; investment-related loss of INR1-2 crore annualised, with profit targeted from next year. Overall international branded business estimated at about INR30 crore; new US listings, Nepal launch and Vietnam test marketing are early-stage seeding.

segments.name: Freeze-dried coffee (FDC)
segments.commentary: Utilisation higher than spray-dried; management expects FDC to reach near full utilisation in 1-1.5 years. Capacity addition of about 6,000 tons per expansion is under consideration, in Vietnam or India.

segments.name: Spray-dried coffee (SDC)
segments.commentary: Adequate capacity for the next 2-3 years per management, with utilisation similar to FDC at group level but lower.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at about 15% (Q2 volume growth 10-15%), with EBITDA growth in tandem at about 15%; management said EBITDA could be a couple of percentage points higher at year-end.
EBITDA per kg expected to stay in the INR135-140 range; no major upward or downward change expected from product mix.

Gross debt guidance of INR1,000-1,200 crore and net debt around INR800 crore maintained; working capital may rise ahead of the Vietnam procurement season, with a precise year-end number to be given at Q3.
Capacity expansion decision (FDC, possibly 6,000 tons) or strategic tie-up expected around end of Q4 FY27 or start of Q1 FY28; FDC lead time 9-12 months.
Capex for a 6,000-ton FDC expansion expected to be about INR500 crore plus inflation, similar to the last expansion.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capacity utilisation about 70%, with freeze-dried utilisation higher; management expects to start capacity expansion at 80-85% utilisation.
Green coffee prices range-bound at about USD3,400-3,800 per ton; Vietnam crop expected Nov-Dec 2026 to set the price trend.
FDC machine supply is not a constraint; roasters sourced from Brazil and Europe, and management expects underwriting of 30-50% of new capacity before committing.
Strategic options under evaluation: contract manufacturing or JV, with decision by end Q4 FY27 or start Q1 FY28.
Funding for expansion expected largely from internal accruals; net debt cushion of about INR300-400 crore cited.
demand_pricing: Volume growth in Q2 was in the 10-15% range; value growth lagged because lower green coffee prices reduced selling prices.
Demand for FDC stronger than SDC globally; FDC share of the mix largely unchanged versus the last 2-3 quarters.
Domestic price cuts on some SKUs after the September 2025 GST cut, offset by price increases on other SKUs due to coffee and energy costs.
Long-term contracts returning as prices fall, though customers are waiting for price stability; daily swings of USD50-100 cited.

Other expenses rose sharply to about INR190-200 crore from about INR140-150 crore, attributed to freight, insurance, higher A&P spend and fuel; management said the rise is passed through on CIF contracts and does not affect per-kg profit.
Single-digit global B2B market share; new clients added in the Far East, and no significant client losses reported.

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth above 15% or in the 10-15% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 volume growth was in the 10-15% range; FY27 guidance of about 15% is on track with Q3 and Q4 order books robust.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA grow slower than volume, and is there a one-off in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant one-off; EBITDA about 10% vs volume 10-15% because the FD/SD mix benefit is now in the base. Growth should move in tandem going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and interest rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt INR1,192 crore and net debt INR742 crore at 30 Sep 2026; average rate about 7-7.5%. Guidance of gross INR1,000-1,200 crore maintained, as working capital may rise ahead of the Vietnam procurement season.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international branded business size?
qa_highlights.answer: Percol expected at INR25-30 crore in FY27; overall international branded about INR30 crore, with other brands at seeding stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lead time and cost of FDC capacity addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Lead time 9-12 months; capacity addition likely about 6,000 tons, with capex about INR500 crore plus inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Will FDC expansion be by contract manufacturing or equity JV?
qa_highlights.answer: Both options are open; any strategic tie-up would need about 30-50% capacity underwriting before a plant is committed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for green coffee prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Vietnam crop reports are mixed (El Nino risk versus reasonable crop so far); clarity expected by December, with prices holding around USD3,700-3,800.

risks_watch: Vietnam crop (Nov-Dec 2026) and El Nino risk could move green coffee prices and working capital needs.
Other expenses running at about INR190-200 crore; watch whether A&P and freight costs normalise in Q3.
Gross margin decline of about 200-300 bps (per analyst calculation) against stable EBITDA per kg; management said gross margin is not a reliable guide given FOB/CIF mix.
Lower forex gain in H1 FY27 (about INR11 crore vs about INR39-40 crore last year) is a headwind to EBITDA comparisons.
Rising interest rates and higher debt as procurement increases; FDC utilisation approaching full in 1-1.5 years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year volume and EBITDA guidance and on balance sheet comfort, but cautious and repeatedly hedged on near-term coffee price direction and on the timing and route of capacity expansion. Management deflected some questions on EBITDA variance and debt reduction, reiterating guidance without changing it.

adds.what: 6,000 ton freeze-dried coffee (FDC) capacity expansion under consideration, Vietnam or India; decision expected end Q4 FY27 or start Q1 FY28

growth.why: Management held FY27 guidance of about 15% volume growth with similar (~15%) EBITDA growth, but Q2 revenue rose only 7.8% and EBITDA 9.5%, and the 6,000-ton FDC expansion is undecided (decision end Q4 FY27, 9-12 month lead time), so near-term growth is backed mainly by demand and existing capacity at ~70% utilisation.
